description:
Measured on develop 01e69178a.

  def main(), do: Enum.each(JSON.decode!("[[1,2]]"), fn r -> IO.inspect(Enum.count(r)) end)

elixir prints 2. fz2 interp and run refuse to compile: error[artifact/incomplete-semantic-plan]: `Enumerable.count/1` has no implementation for the value it is called with. The same happens with Enum.to_list(r) and Enum.map(r, f) (the refusal names `Enumerable.reduce/3`). Enum.join(r) is refused one step earlier, as error[spec/violation] for arguments ({any, any}) against its list domain.

What works: Enum.count(hd(JSON.decode!("[[1,2]]"))) prints 2, and so does the value half of a map entry, Enum.each(JSON.decode!("{\"k\":[1,2]}"), fn {_, r} -> Enum.count(r) end).

So the trigger is the element type Enum.each hands its function when the enumerable is any: it includes the Map impl s {key, value} pair, a tuple, which has no Enumerable impl. A protocol call whose receiver type has one member without an impl is refused at compile time. Elixir decides at run time and raises Protocol.UndefinedError only when such a value actually arrives (Enum.count(1): protocol Enumerable not implemented for Integer).

Two parts:
1. A protocol call on a receiver type that some members implement and some do not compiles; the members without an impl raise Protocol.UndefinedError at run time, as in Elixir. A receiver type that NO member implements can stay a compile-time refusal.
2. Enum.join/1,2 take Enumerable.t(a), not [a]. Spiked: widening the two specs alone moves the join repro from the spec violation to the refusal in part 1, so part 1 comes first. About forty other public Enum functions also declare a list first argument (at, chunk_by, chunk_every, concat, dedup, dedup_by, fetch, fetch!, frequencies, frequencies_by, group_by, max, min, max_by, min_by, min_max, min_max_by, product, sum, sum_by, sort_by, uniq, uniq_by, unzip, zip, zip_with, count_until); check each against Elixir.

Part 1 touches how Protocol.UndefinedError is raised, which fz-3sy.8 (session fz-da) is changing; coordinate before building.

Not on the distiller s path: tests/distill_telemetry_test.rs passes on develop with this open.

Repros: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz-xxd13-build/d6960461-b7a2-4585-a9e7-9f2477e57ee2/scratchpad/b141/ (a.fz and c.fz pass; b.fz, d.fz, e.fz, f.fz are refused; f.fz is the case Elixir raises on at run time).
title: An element of an any enumerable is accepted by Enum's functions, as in Elixir
